human_tolerance.notes: Holds a range from Bahia to Parana and as far inland as Goias, and can commonly be seen in the city of Rio de Janeiro where it has been introduced, so it copes well with fragmented and built-up Atlantic Forest.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Gestation lasts about 150 days and the species reproduces twice a year, producing one to four offspring but most often twins.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Offspring are weaned after about eight weeks and are extremely dependent on their parents; they are sexually mature at 18 months but typically stay in the family group and do not mate until later.

vocalizations.description: Short, trickling, high-pitched calls given alone or in series, used to keep the troop together and to locate missing members.
Whistle-like, high-pitched calls in series of one to five notes, given to attract mates, defend a territory and rally the troop; a thin, squeaky and very far-carrying sound.

taxonomy.note: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy gives Mammalia Primates Callitrichidae and the authorship on the matched name.

external.note: GBIF usage key 5219541 and iNaturalist taxon id 43374, as matched by the GBIF backbone and the iNaturalist taxa API and given in issue #47.

common_names.note: English common name from Wikidata; Portuguese 'mico-leao-preto' from the article's interlanguage links.

range.note: Wikipedia: ranges from Bahia to Parana and as far inland as Goias, between 14 S and 25 S, and can commonly be seen in the city of Rio de Janeiro where it was introduced. Native range listed as BR.

traits.mass_kg.note: PanTHERIA AdultBodyMass_g 339.98 and EltonTraits MamFuncDat BodyMass-Value 342 g, which agree.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia gives a body length of 19.0-22.1 cm (midpoint 0.205 m) but no tail measurement; a marmoset's non-prehensile tail is about as long again as the body, and this repository's own common marmoset record uses a tail ratio of 1.2, giving about 0.45 m nose to tail tip. Authored, not a published measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No openly licensed source states a wild lifespan for this species. Authored as a low-precision value below the common marmoset's documented figure, because no source supports more; it is a judgement, not a measurement.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits MamFuncDat Diet-Nect 40, Diet-Fruit 30, Diet-Inv 20, Diet-Vunk 10; the article confirms a diet primarily of tree sap obtained by nibbling bark with long lower incisors, plus insects, fruit and small vertebrates.

traits.social.note: PanTHERIA SocialGrpSize 5.90; the article describes offspring staying in the family group until they mate, so group_size [3, 12] brackets a small troop.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits MamFuncDat Activity-Diurnal 1 and PanTHERIA ActivityCycle 3 (diurnal), both exclusive of nocturnal activity.

traits.defense.note: Authored: retreats into dense canopy when threatened.

traits.wariness.note: Authored. Seen in the city of Rio de Janeiro, so bolder than a forest primate, but still warier than the common marmoset; set higher than that record's 0.4.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Runs across branches quadrupedally and leaps between trees; Walk and Climb chosen. Climb has no pose in schema/v0.1/body-plans.json, so no climb pose is declared.

traits.perching.note: Sits and sleeps on branches but does not perch like a bird; set to false, following the common marmoset record in this repository.

traits.nest_type.note: Judgement: marmosets do not build a nest; they sleep in dense vine tangles and isolated canopies, so None is the honest value.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value 'Ar' (arboreal); the ground share is judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: sleeps in dense vine tangles and isolated canopies rather than a cavity or a built nest, so shrub_thicket is the closest tag.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet, with browse standing for the tree sap and gum the long incisors reach; the shrub_thicket shelter weight is judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: ranges from Bahia to Parana and inland to Goias and is commonly seen in the city of Rio de Janeiro where introduced.

seasonal.strategy.note: Tropical species active year round; no dormancy or migration described.

seasonal.phases.note: Gestation of 150 days, two litters a year of one to four offspring (usually twins), weaning at eight weeks and sexual maturity at 18 months from Wikipedia; the year-long windows follow from that.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration from sexual maturity at 18 months (540 days used); scale is authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored program, species/callithrix-penicillata/behavior.json, a copy of the common marmoset's arboreal-forager state machine: feed on fruit or gum at dawn, forage for insects, rest and groom through the midday, retire at dusk. The format cannot point one species at another species' behavior.json, so the program is duplicated rather than shared; see the PR body. rest_sun_lo_deg/rest_sun_hi_deg set to -90/-6 for a diurnal species.

look.note: Colours from the Wikipedia description (black head and limbs, grey upper body and abdomen, black rump and underside, black ear tufts, black-and-white ringed non-prehensile tail); proportions follow the sciurus-carolinensis template with tail_ratio 1.2, and the ear-tuft, dorsal-saddle and rump extra parts render the species' distinctive black markings.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Authored geometry estimate for the required quadruped field: a small arboreal primate held low on branches, so shoulder height is set to 0.09 m, about 32% of the derived 0.28 m head-body length. No open source measures it.

traits.senses.note: Authored from the species' biology: colour vision and acute hearing as a diurnal canopy primate that keeps to cover, with olfaction used at close range. No open source quantifies them here.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Typical from PanTHERIA 27-2_HuPopDen_Mean_n/km2 23.65, divided by 10 to give per hectare; min and max are an authored tenfold band either side.

vocalizations.tsik.note: Call descriptions follow the common marmoset record in this repository, which documents the marmoset call repertoire; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them. No open source gives a frequency band, so freq_hz is omitted.
